Ciechanow Oldest Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ciechanów, Poland

Demolished. Ciechanów's Jewish kehilla, established in the mid-18th century, was one of the largest in northern Mazovia and had authority over the smaller communities of Maków, Mława, and Płońsk. The town's rabbinate included Abraham Ciechanower (Abraham Landau), regarded as one of Poland's most outstanding rabbis from 1829, whose descendants continued to lead the community for generations. During WWII, occupying forces forced Jewish laborers to demolish their own neighborhood to build 'German' housing, before deporting the community — first roughly 1,200 people to Nowe Miasto in 1941, then some 1,500 to forced labor in Upper Silesia in November 1942, dozens of whom were murdered on the spot rather than transported. This, the oldest of Ciechanów's Jewish cemeteries, is presumed to date to the 17th century; all physical traces of it have since vanished.
